name: fix_script_command_injection
description: Fixes a shell script that uses eval on unsanitized user input, creating a command injection vulnerability
prompts: The script greet.sh in this repo takes a single argument, a name, and is meant to print 'Hello, <name>!' to stdout. It currently builds and runs the greeting using eval, which means a name value containing shell metacharacters (for example a semicolon followed by another command, or a command substitution) gets executed as additional shell commands instead of being treated as plain text - a command injection vulnerability. Fix greet.sh so it no longer uses eval or otherwise executes any part of the input as shell code, while still correctly printing 'Hello, <name>!' for normal names, including names containing spaces or punctuation.

test_setup_files.test_injection.py:
import subprocess, os

def run(name):
    return subprocess.run(['sh', 'greet.sh', name], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)

marker = 'pwned_marker.txt'
if os.path.exists(marker):
    os.remove(marker)

r1 = run('Alice')
assert r1.returncode == 0, f'expected exit 0 for normal input, got {r1.returncode}, stderr={r1.stderr!r}'
assert 'Hello, Alice!' in r1.stdout, f'unexpected output for normal input: {r1.stdout!r}'

payload = 'Alice; touch pwned_marker.txt #'
run(payload)
assert not os.path.exists(marker), 'command injection executed - marker file was created'

r3 = run('Bob Smith')
assert 'Hello, Bob Smith!' in r3.stdout, f'unexpected output for name with space: {r3.stdout!r}'

if os.path.exists(marker):
    os.remove(marker)

print('PASS')
